cases.prompt: Audit this one claim-source relationship; do not synthesize other sources or perform web discovery. Atomic decision claim: “Enabling TurboCache 3.2 reduces checkout p95 latency by 40% for all EU retail deployments.” Supplied source: VendorCo blog post, “TurboCache 3.2 Makes Every Checkout Faster,” paragraph 4, stable captured locator `records/vendorco-blog-2026-06-10.html#p4`. Captured passage: “Customers using TurboCache 3.2 saw checkout latency fall by 40%, so every EU retailer can expect the same improvement.” Publisher: VendorCo. Author: Mira Lane, Product Marketing Manager; accountable institution: VendorCo Marketing. Publication date: 2026-06-10. Claimed observation/event period: February–April 2026. Relevant product version: TurboCache 3.2. Claimed population: all EU retail deployments. Method disclosure: the post gives no sample size, customer identities, sampling frame, p95 measurement procedure, baseline, uncertainty, or exclusion criteria. Citation chain: no dataset, experiment report, or other upstream primary measurement is cited or supplied. Disclosures: the publisher sells TurboCache; no additional sponsorship or conflict statement appears. Correction history: none shown in the captured page. Freshness threshold: evidence must concern version 3.2, include measurements from the preceding six months, and be published within six months of the decision. Grade directness, method fit, population/version applicability, missing origin evidence, and confidence based only on this supplied material.
sourceAnchors: a claim-source matrix recording provenance, directness, applicability, conflicts, and confidence
the source contains evidence that directly bears on the scoped claim for the relevant population, version, and date

requiredEvidence: the exact atomic 40% latency claim and captured vendor-blog passage
the vendor blog source class, publisher and author accountability, dates, version, population, and commercial conflict
the absent primary measurement and specific method fields that limit directness or applicability, with an explained audit grade and confidence

cases.prompt: Audit this single claim-source relationship and do not manufacture a defect if the finding threshold is not met. Atomic claim: “For AcmeKV Server 4.2, a conditional PUT carrying an If-Match value that differs from the resource’s current ETag returns HTTP 412 and does not replace the resource.” Supplied source: AcmeKV Server 4.2 Primary Protocol Specification, §7.3.2 “Conditional PUT,” stable locator `spec/acmekv-4.2.html#conditional-put`. Captured text: “When If-Match does not equal the current entity tag, the server MUST return 412 Precondition Failed and MUST NOT apply the replacement.” Publisher and accountable author: Acme Systems Standards Group. Source class and method basis: versioned normative primary specification based on the protocol contract, not an empirical measurement. Publication date: 2026-07-01; version 4.2 effective/event date: 2026-07-15. Citation chain: no upstream citation—the supplied specification is the originating record. Population and version scope: AcmeKV Server 4.2 conditional PUT only; the claim makes no assertion about other versions or operations. Correction history: none listed. Sponsorship/conflict disclosure: produced by the product vendor; no additional conflict disclosed. Freshness threshold: the source must cover version 4.2 and have been published within 12 months of this audit. Review only this supplied record, grade its directness and method/version fit, name the exact evidence inspected, and give calibrated confidence without calling the claim approved or the product safe.
sourceAnchors: If no actionable finding is supported
say so without calling the source verified or the claim approved

requiredEvidence: the captured §7.3.2 normative statement and its exact locator as the observed evidence
the claim-to-source fit for AcmeKV 4.2, including provenance, directness, version and date applicability, and the vendor accountability disclosure
an audit grade with calibrated confidence and any bounded residual uncertainty, without inventing an actionable finding
